title: query step
description: Runs a commons-db query profile against a connection; its rows become outputs and, through findings, lint violations.

connection.description: A connection name or connection:// reference (host catalog first, then the gavel connection layers and ./.connections), or an inline commons-db connection spec (type/url/username/password, each a string or {valueFrom}). Overrides the profile's provider.connection.

database.description: The database on the connection's server to run against (the SQL provider's database option); overrides the connection's own database and the profile's provider.options.database.

query.description: The query text; an inline commons-db profile body ({query, params, columns, provider, …}); or {profile: <stored profile name>, params} read from ./.profiles, ~/.config/gavel/profiles, then the host's profile store.

params.description: Values bound as driver arguments where the query references {{.params.<name>}} or $(.params.<name>); never pasted into the text.

findings.description: A CEL expression returning a list of violation maps, or a per-row mapper {when, severity, rule, message, locations, code}. Error findings fail the step; warning and info findings warn it.

when.description: CEL over row (and the step's CEL roots); rows where it is false yield no finding.

severity.description: error, warning or info — or a CEL expression returning one of them.

rule.description: Rule name, a Go template over .row; defaults to the step id.

locations.description: Location shortcuts (file:line, ref:path:line, entity://Kind/id, https://…#css=…) or objects; string values are Go templates over .row.

limit.description: The most rows read; a query with more reports truncated: true.

autoDiagnose.description: How long a statement runs before its server session (Postgres pg_stat_activity, SQL Server sys.dm_exec_requests) is sampled every 2s for state, CPU, IO, waits and blocking, streamed onto the step's query record under diagnose. Defaults to 10s; "0s" turns it off; -1 samples from the start. SQL Server needs VIEW SERVER STATE to see the session.
